_comment: PEOPLE YOU TRUST, checked for anything that touches your positions.
_how_to_add: Put the handle in the right list. Bluesky handles look like 'name.bsky.social' or a custom domain. Delete anything that gets noisy — this is a trust list, so it is meant to be short and yours.
_why_not_twitter: X removed free API access; the cheapest tier that can read posts is roughly $100-200 a month, and scraping around it means a login wall, datacentre blocking and a terms-of-service breach that would break quietly a few weeks later. Rather than ship something that looks like it works and silently stops, X is left unbuilt. If you ever decide the subscription is worth it, `accounts.py` takes a second source without restructuring — the handles, the relevance filter and the seen-post memory are all source-agnostic.
_bluesky_examples: Add handles here, one per line, no @ sign. For example a financial journalist you
read, a central-bank watcher, a foreign-affairs reporter. Free, no key, no login.
_relevance: A post is pushed only if it names one of your holdings, a company you watch, or a theme keyword below. Everything else is ignored — a trusted account posting about lunch is still lunch.
_limits: max_per_run caps how many notifications one run can send, so a busy news day cannot flood your phone. Posts already seen are never re-sent.
